entities.name: American Baptist Churches USA
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
American Baptist Churches USA (ABC-USA), established in its current form as the American Baptist Convention in 1907 (building on the Triennial Convention founded in 1814 — America's first national Protestant organization), is one of the oldest and largest Baptist denominations in the United States with approximately 1.3 million members and a theologically and racially diverse tradition historically associated with religious liberty, abolition, and social justice.

The Triennial Convention of 1814 — the first national Protestant cooperative body in America — was founded partly through the efforts of Adoniram Judson and Luther Rice, who had converted to Baptist beliefs en route to India as Congregationalist missionaries. This founding marked American Baptists' entrance into organized international missions. The convention split in 1845 over slavery — Southern Baptists withdrew to form the Southern Baptist Convention — leaving the Northern/American Baptists with a more diverse and progressive theological tradition.

ABC-USA has historically been associated with social justice causes: it was integrated before the Civil Rights Movement (though never without tension), maintained women in ministry, and produced important 20th-century social gospel theologians. Martin Luther King Jr. came from the Black Baptist tradition closely linked to American Baptist fellowship. The denomination's Valley Forge, Pennsylvania headquarters coordinates 5,000+ congregations spanning significant racial diversity — reflecting the ABC-USA's position as one of America's most theologically inclusive major Baptist bodies.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: American Baptist Churches USA — tracing from America's first national Protestant cooperative body (1814), defined by its anti-slavery stance in the 1845 split, and maintaining a theologically inclusive social justice tradition — is a foundational institution in American Protestant denominational history.
